title: Peeling Apart That Supposed $120 Billion Chip Deal Google Inked With Marvell
gist: The widely-reported '$120 billion Google-Marvell chip deal' is actually a warrant-based structure where Google gets discretionary stock options tied to purchase milestones through 2033, not a locked-in spend commitment; Marvell's stock pop on the announcement already exceeded the warrants' value before a single chip shipped, revealing a circular financial-engineering dynamic layered on top of genuine custom-silicon programs (an inference LPU code-named Merope and a memory/CXL product possibly code-named Kestrel).

themes.theme: Deal structure is looser than headlines suggest

insights.claim: The headline framing of a '$120 billion' Google-Marvell deal (Marvell getting $120B in sales/work, Google investing $12.5B in Marvell stock) is misleading because the actual mechanism is a share warrant agreement, not a firm purchase or investment commitment.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors modeling this as guaranteed $120B revenue for Marvell or a $12.5B cash outlay from Google should instead treat it as a contingent, revenue-triggered equity option structure with real optionality for Google to walk away.
insights.quote: the deal is a bit more slippery than it has been reported
insights.locator: Here's the deal paragraph

insights.claim: Per Marvell's 8-K filing with the SEC, the companies entered a commercial agreement for Marvell's development of 'Custom Products' for Google spanning AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute, all attaching to the TPU ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: This defines Marvell's actual scope of work inside Google's TPU supply chain — a multi-product custom silicon program, not a single chip — useful for sizing Marvell's addressable content per TPU rack.
insights.quote: The expanded partnership spans a comprehensive range of custom silicon programs that attach to the TPU ecosystem, including AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute.
insights.locator: 8-K filing paragraph

insights.claim: Google holds warrants for 58.97 million Marvell shares that, once fully vested, would give it 6.3 percent ownership of Marvell.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 6.3% equity stake would make Google one of Marvell's largest shareholders, giving it potential board influence over a key AI infrastructure supplier — a governance angle beyond the commercial contract.
insights.locator: By the way, those warrants paragraph

insights.claim: Of the warrant shares, 1.36 million vest across the first four quarters, and the remaining shares vest in 240 buckets, with each bucket tied to $500 million of Marvell revenue billed to Google.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: This ties Marvell's equity upside directly to realized Google purchase orders (roughly $500M increments), giving a concrete way to reverse-engineer Marvell's Google-derived revenue run rate from future 8-K vesting disclosures.
insights.locator: By the way, those warrants paragraph

insights.claim: Google is not obligated to exercise the warrants: it can wait until August 18, 2033 to convert vested shares, and if it never exercises and Marvell's share price is below a floor of $206.58, the shares simply expire worthless.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The deal is asymmetric optionality for Google, not a binding investment — Marvell bears execution risk on custom silicon delivery while Google retains full discretion on whether to ever convert the warrants into actual equity spend.
insights.locator: Here is the funny bit about this deal paragraph

insights.claim: Marvell's market capitalization rose $18.6 billion on the day the deal was announced, an amount that already exceeds the $12.5 billion headline value of Google's warrants — meaning the deal effectively 'paid for itself' in market value before any component under the agreement had shipped.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Illustrates how AI infrastructure deal announcements are generating value primarily through market re-rating and stock-price reflexivity rather than delivered product — a pattern investors should discount when assessing 'deal size' headlines across the sector.
insights.quote: the $18.6 billion rise in Marvell's stock price the day the deal was announced more than covers the $12.5 billion value of the warrants, so in a way, the deal has already paid for itself and not a single component has shipped under the deal
insights.locator: Neither Google nor Marvell have commented paragraph

insights.claim: The deal functions as a financial roundtrip: Google effectively pays ~$500 million per quarter for Marvell stock exposure over six years to secure the partnership, but the very existence of the deal drives Marvell's stock up, and Google's resulting equity gains act as a rebate that offsets what it pays Marvell for chip shepherding work.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A reusable framework for decoding hyperscaler-supplier 'mega deals': structured warrant/equity arrangements let buyers recapture part of their capex as paper equity gains, inflating the apparent scale and mutual benefit of the deal beyond its cash economics.
insights.quote: The increasing share of the rise in market cap that Google will gain ... is a kind of rebate on paying Marvell to do chip shepherding.
insights.locator: Google pays for $500 million a quarter paragraph

insights.claim: The paper equity gains Google books from its Marvell warrants strengthen Google's balance sheet, which in turn helps Google raise private debt to further fund its AI infrastructure buildout — some of which flows back to Marvell as more custom-chip business, closing a self-reinforcing loop.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Signals a broader financing pattern in the GenAI buildout where supplier equity stakes are being used indirectly as balance-sheet collateral for hyperscaler debt issuance — worth tracking in Google's and peers' debt raises and covenant structures.
insights.quote: Google pays real money for the chippery and gets a kind of funny money that strengthens its balance sheet back, and that helps Google be better able to raise private debt to further invest in hardware for the GenAI buildout, which helps Marvell.
insights.locator: Google pays for $500 million a quarter paragraph

insights.claim: The author expects Google will not let its Marvell warrants lapse worthless, because Google wants both board-level influence at Marvell and the balance-sheet benefit ('funny money') to help fund its AI buildout over the next five years.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Suggests Google is likely to become a long-term strategic equity holder in Marvell rather than a purely transactional customer, which could support Marvell's valuation floor near the $206.58 warrant strike price through 2033.
insights.quote: I doubt very much that Google will do that, wanting both influence on the Marvell board and also wanting to help cover the costs of its AI buildout in the next five years with Marvell funny money.
insights.locator: Here is the funny bit about this deal paragraph

insights.claim: Trade and business press widely reported that the Google-Marvell deal includes a code-named 'Merope' chip, characterized as a language processing unit (LPU) specialized for the decode phase of GenAI inference (generating the response) as distinct from the prefill phase (processing the prompt/context).
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: An LPU dedicated to low-latency decode would be a distinct product category from Google's TPUs, implying Google is diversifying its silicon portfolio to cover inference latency weaknesses rather than relying on TPUs for the full inference pipeline.
insights.locator: All of the trade press paragraph

insights.claim: The Information reported in April that Google was in talks with Marvell on two chips: the Merope LPU, and a separate memory processor possibly built as a CXL-based memory area network letting TPU systems share DRAM as a caching tier, reducing the DRAM needed per host.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A shared/disaggregated memory tier via CXL would materially cut per-server DRAM bill-of-materials for TPU pods — a direct lever on Google's infrastructure capex per unit of AI compute.
insights.locator: The Information reported back in April paragraph

insights.claim: DRAM memory prices have risen 7.1x over the past year, making a CXL-based shared-memory architecture for TPU systems 'absolutely necessary' rather than merely nice-to-have, according to the author.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable macro data point: extreme DRAM price inflation (7.1x YoY) is a direct cost driver forcing hyperscalers toward memory-disaggregation architectures — relevant to memory chipmakers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) and CXL-ecosystem suppliers as a demand catalyst.
insights.quote: DRAM memory prices already up 7.1X in the past year
insights.locator: The Information reported back in April paragraph

insights.claim: Neither Google nor Marvell has officially confirmed the Merope chip rumors; the name 'Merope' does not even appear in the deal's addendum documents.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors should treat 'Merope' reporting as unconfirmed market rumor, not a disclosed roadmap item, when assessing near-term revenue tied to this specific chip.
insights.quote: Neither Google nor Marvell have commented on these rumors.
insights.locator: The Information reported back in April paragraph

insights.claim: The deal addendum instead names a product code-named 'Kestrel,' which Google wants qualified no later than November 10, 2027; the author speculates this could be the memory server/CXL product rather than Merope.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: November 2027 is a concrete milestone date to watch for confirmation of Google's next custom-silicon product tied to the TPU ecosystem; a slip or confirmation here would validate or undercut current market speculation about the deal's real technical content.
insights.locator: Here is the other funny bit paragraph

insights.claim: The name 'Kestrel' is confusingly reused: Google separately has a 'Project Kestrel' referring to a cluster of hyperscale datacenters being built in the Kansas City, Missouri region.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Signals a naming collision investors should not conflate: the chip-deal 'Kestrel' and the datacenter-campus 'Kestrel' are (per the author's read) related but distinct entities, and confusing them risks mispricing the scope of either.
insights.quote: Just to be confusing – or maybe not – Google has another Project Kestrel, which is the codename for a series of datacenters being built in its Kansas City, Missouri region
insights.locator: Here is the other funny bit paragraph

insights.claim: Google's Project Kestrel datacenter campus in the Kansas City, Missouri region spans roughly 430 acres and will hold up to five hyperscale datacenters worth around $100 billion, totaling about 2.5 million square feet of aggregate capacity (revised up from earlier rumors of six datacenters and 1.8 million square feet).
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A ~$100 billion single-region datacenter buildout is a major concrete data point for tracking Google's capex concentration and regional power/land demand in the US Midwest — relevant for utilities, REITs, and construction suppliers tied to Kansas City.
insights.locator: Here is the other funny bit paragraph

insights.claim: TPUs are good at AI training and the prefill portion of inference, but the author suggests they (like GPUs and AWS Trainium chips) may not be well suited to the low-latency decode portion of inference — a gap that a dedicated LPU or inference-accelerator chip would fill.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Frames a structural weakness shared across TPUs, GPUs, and Trainium at the decode stage of inference — a reusable lens for evaluating whether any hyperscaler's in-house accelerator strategy is complete without a dedicated low-latency inference chip.
insights.quote: TPUs (which are good for AI training and prefill but maybe not so good at decode at low latency, much as GPUs and Trainiums are also not)
insights.locator: So the Kestrel product launch paragraph

insights.claim: The author's working hypothesis is that the Kestrel chip is the custom AI inference accelerator destined for the Kestrel datacenters, effectively turning that Kansas City campus into a massive clustered AI inference accelerator complex.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: If correct, this ties Marvell's custom-silicon revenue directly to the buildout schedule of a specific ~$100B datacenter campus, giving investors a concrete regional/timeline proxy for Marvell's Google-derived inference-chip revenue ramp.
insights.quote: I think Kestrel is the custom chip that goes into the Kestrel datacenters. In essence, the Kestrel datacenters are a massive clustered AI inference accelerator.
insights.locator: So the Kestrel product launch paragraph

insights.claim: The author predicts the Kestrel accelerator chips will be qualified for deployment in late 2027 and roll into completed datacenters in 2028, with Marvell shepherding them through Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) foundries and packaging, though he characterizes this explicitly as a hunch rather than confirmed fact.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Gives investors a testable timeline (chip qualification late 2027, datacenter production 2028) against which to track TSMC advanced-packaging capacity allocation and Marvell's custom-silicon revenue recognition for the Google program.
insights.quote: It is reasonable for the Kestrel accelerators to be qualified for deployment in late 2027, and they roll into the completed datacenters in 2028 as Marvell shepherds them through the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co foundries and packaging. But that is just human intelligence inference, called a hunch.
insights.locator: closing paragraph

insights.claim: The custom Marvell-shepherded chippery and off-the-shelf components covered by this deal are used in Google Cloud infrastructure, and some of it is expected to appear in TPU systems sold onward to third-party AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Extends the deal's relevance beyond Google's own compute needs: Marvell's custom silicon could indirectly capture revenue exposure to OpenAI's and Anthropic's compute demand growth via Google Cloud TPU sales to those labs.
insights.quote: This gear is used in Google Cloud, and some of it will no doubt appear in TPU systems being sold to the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic.
insights.locator: Google pays for $500 million a quarter paragraph

insights.claim: This Google-Marvell arrangement is characterized by the author as 'another kind of roundtrip' in the current GenAI infrastructure investment frenzy, implying it fits a recognizable pattern seen elsewhere in the industry of vendor-financing-like circular deal structures.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Investors evaluating any hyperscaler/chipmaker mega-deal announcement in this cycle should check for similar circular equity-for-revenue structures before taking headline deal-size figures at face value.
insights.quote: This deal is another kind of roundtrip in this GenAI frenzy.
insights.locator: Neither Google nor Marvell have commented paragraph
